ENGLISH: The Valley of Elah
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 以拉谷

ENGLISH: David & Goliath
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 大卫与歌利亚

ENGLISH: A shepherd boy walks into a valley where an entire army has been silent for forty days.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 一个牧童走进山谷，而整支军队已经在这里沉默了四十天。

ENGLISH: c. 1020 BC, in the Valley of Elah. The Israelite army and the Philistine army are camped on two ridges with a valley between them, and neither side has moved for forty days.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 约公元前 1020 年，以拉谷。以色列和非利士两支军队隔着山谷扎营，四十天来谁也没有动手。

ENGLISH: King Saul commands Israel. The Philistines have a champion named Goliath — close to three metres tall, in bronze scale armour, with a spear shaft like a weaver’s beam. Nobody in Israel will go out to him.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 以色列这边由扫罗王率领；非利士那边有一位名叫歌利亚的巨人，身高近三米，全身铜甲，枪杆粗得像织布的机轴，天天下来叫阵。以色列没有一个人敢出去。

ENGLISH: Both sides agreed to a deal: one fighter each, and the losing nation becomes servants. You are in the camp as a witness. You cannot change the ending — only what you do with the forty days.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 两边讲好了：各派一人单挑，输的那一国举国做奴仆。你是随军的一个见证者。结局你改不了，但在四十天里你要做什么、成为什么样的人，由你决定。

ENGLISH: David refuses Saul’s armour, takes five smooth stones from the brook, and faces Goliath with a sling. The point of the story is not that a small person can be brave — it is that the battle belongs to the LORD.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 大卫脱下扫罗借给他的盔甲，从溪里捡了五块光滑的石子，用甩石的机弦迎上去。这个故事要说的不是「小人物也能赢」，而是这场仗本来就属于耶和华。

ENGLISH: You did not lift a stone. You learned where to look.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 石子不是你甩出去的。你真正学到的，是眼睛该往哪儿看。

ENGLISH: David’s courage came before his confidence: he remembered what God had already done with the lion and the bear. Faith grows by remembering.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 大卫的勇气不是天生的。他先是想起神怎样救他脱离狮子和熊，然后才敢走向那个巨人。信心就是在回忆里一点点长出来的。

ENGLISH: Think of one “giant” in your life right now. What is the first step of faith for you?
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你生命里现在有一个什么样的「巨人」？信心的第一步，对你来说会是什么？

ENGLISH: Remember what God has already brought me through
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 先回想神已经带我走过的路

ENGLISH: That is exactly where David started — not with the giant, but with the lion and the bear behind him. 1 Samuel 17:37
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 大卫就是这样开始的——不是从巨人开始，而是从身后的狮子和熊开始。撒母耳记上 17:37

ENGLISH: Tell someone, so I am not facing it alone
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 找一个人说出口，不要一个人扛

ENGLISH: Wise. Even David asked questions of the whole line before he stepped forward. 1 Samuel 17:26
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 这是智慧。大卫出阵以前，也先跟阵上的人说过话。撒母耳记上 17:26

ENGLISH: Refuse armour that does not fit me and simply start
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 脱掉别人给我的盔甲，用自己的方式上

ENGLISH: Saul’s armour was excellent — for Saul. Discernment is knowing which help is actually yours to carry. 1 Samuel 17:39
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 扫罗的盔甲很好——只是不合大卫。分辨力，就是分得清哪些帮助真的适合你。撒母耳记上 17:39

ENGLISH: The scroll grows warm in your hands. The ink shifts, campfires flicker into being, and the smell of dust and sheep fills the air.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 书卷在你手里发烫，墨迹像水一样流动。营火一盏一盏亮起来，尘土和羊群的气味扑到脸上。

ENGLISH: A man in a travel-stained scribe’s robe steps beside you. This is Corin, your companion on the road.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 有人在你身边站定，是个满身风尘、穿文士长袍的人。他叫柯林，此后一路与你同行。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: The Valley of Elah, around 1020 BC. Hear me clearly: we are witnesses. We cannot rewrite what God has written. But we can choose what kind of people we become while we watch.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「公元前一〇二〇年左右，以拉谷。」他低声说，「记住：我们只是见证人，改不了神写下的结局。能决定的，是我们自己成为怎样的人。」

SPEAKER: soldier
ENGLISH: Forty days. Forty mornings that giant has shouted at us, and not one man has answered.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 山谷对面，非利士人的军队已经骂阵四十天。四十天里，以色列没有一个人出去应战。

SPEAKER: goliath
ENGLISH: Choose a man for yourselves, and let him come down to me! If he be able to fight with me and kill me, then will we be your servants — but if I prevail, then shall ye be our servants!
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「你们拣选一个人，叫他下来到我这里来！他若能与我交战，把我杀了，我们就作你们的仆人。」

ENGLISH: The whole line of Israel shifts backward. Corin looks at you. So — where will you stand?
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 喊声撞在两边山壁上。以色列全军往后退了一步。柯林看着你：你要站在哪里？

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: Every choice here will leave a mark on you, not on the story. That is how the road works.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 这里每一个选择，刻下来的都是你自己，不是故事。这条路的规矩就是这样。

ENGLISH: Walk to the front line and face the shouting
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 走到最前线去，迎着那声音

ENGLISH: Your legs do not feel brave, but they carry you forward. The giant’s voice fills your chest — and you stay.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你一点也不觉得自己勇敢，可你还是一步一步往前走。巨人的吼声压在胸口上——你没有退，就那样站着。

ENGLISH: Ask Corin what the Law says about fear
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 问柯林，律法怎么说「不要怕」

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: Corin opens his scroll. “The officers shall say to the people: let not your hearts faint, fear not — for the LORD your God goeth with you.” You had heard it before. Today you need it.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 柯林展开书卷：「官长又要对百姓说：你们不要胆怯，不要惧怕他们，因为耶和华你们的神与你们同去。」

ENGLISH: Find the soldiers who are shaking and sit with them
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 到发抖的士兵中间坐下

ENGLISH: You sit in the dust beside a boy no older than sixteen. He stops trembling long enough to share his bread. Courage is easier when you are not alone.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你在一名不到十六岁的少年兵旁边坐下。他不再发抖，把自己仅有的饼掰了一半给你。

ENGLISH: A young man comes up the ridge from the baggage train, leading a donkey loaded with bread and cheese. He is small, sun-browned, and entirely unnoticed.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 一个年轻人从辎重营那边爬上山脊，牵着一头驮着饼和奶酪的驴。他个子不高，晒得黝黑，没有谁多看他一眼。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: That is David, the youngest son of Jesse. He has been sent to bring food to his brothers. He was not invited to the battle.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 那是大卫，耶西最小的儿子。父亲派他来给几个哥哥送吃的——没有人叫他来打仗。

SPEAKER: goliath
ENGLISH: I defy the armies of Israel this day! Give me a man, that we may fight together!
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「我今日向以色列人的军队骂阵。你们叫一个人出来，与我交战吧！」

ENGLISH: David stops. His head tilts. He is listening — not to the size of the giant, but to what the giant is saying about God.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 大卫停住脚步，侧过头去听。他听的不是那巨人有多壮，而是他在怎样谈论神。

ENGLISH: Tell David the king has offered a great reward
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 告诉大卫，王悬了重赏

SPEAKER: david
ENGLISH: David nods, but you can tell the reward is not what has caught him. He keeps looking at the giant.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 大卫点点头，可你看得出来，让他动心的不是赏钱。他的眼睛始终没离开那巨人。

ENGLISH: Warn him that the whole army is afraid
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 提醒他全军都在害怕

SPEAKER: david
ENGLISH: You tell him plainly. David looks down the line of frightened men. “I see,” he says. He does not step back.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你照实说了。大卫望了望那排惊惶的人：「我看见了。」他没有往后退。

ENGLISH: Ask him about the lion and the bear
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 问起狮子和熊的事

SPEAKER: david
ENGLISH: His whole face changes. “The LORD that delivered me out of the paw of the lion and out of the paw of the bear — he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine.”
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他整张脸都亮了：「耶和华救我脱离狮子和熊的爪，也必救我脱离这非利士人的手。」

ENGLISH: Word travels fast through a bored army. Within the hour David is standing in the tent of King Saul.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 营里的消息传得比人快。不到一个时辰，大卫已经站在扫罗的帐棚里。

SPEAKER: saul
ENGLISH: Thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him: for thou art but a youth, and he a man of war from his youth.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「你不能去与那非利士人交战，因为你年纪太轻，他从小就作战士。」

SPEAKER: david
ENGLISH: Thy servant kept his father’s sheep, and there came a lion and a bear, and took a lamb out of the flock. Thy servant slew both the lion and the bear. This uncircumcised Philistine shall be as one of them, seeing he hath defied the armies of the living God.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「你仆人为父亲放羊。有时来了狮子，有时来了熊，从羊群里叼走一只羊羔，你仆人就把狮子和熊都打死了。」

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: Saul has armour. It is the best in Israel. Watch what happens next.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 扫罗把自己的盔甲给大卫穿上——那是全以色列最好的一套。

ENGLISH: Offer David your own walking staff
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 把你的手杖递给大卫

SPEAKER: david
ENGLISH: He thanks you, smiling, and hands it gently back. “I have not proved these,” he says of the king’s armour. He takes his staff, his bag, and nothing else.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他笑着道谢，又轻轻还回你手里：「这些我从来没试过。」说完转身往溪边去了。

ENGLISH: Urge him to take the king’s sword anyway
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 劝他还是带上王的刀

SPEAKER: david
ENGLISH: He fastens it, takes two steps, and nearly falls. “I cannot go with these.” He unbuckles it. Corin raises an eyebrow at you.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他佩上刀，走了两步，差点绊倒：「穿这些我走不了路。」于是把刀解下来。柯林忍住笑，什么也没说。

ENGLISH: Say nothing. Watch what he does.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 什么也不说，看他怎么做

ENGLISH: A borrowed identity never fits in the valley. David walks out in a shepherd’s tunic.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 借来的身份，穿在身上总不合身。大卫穿着牧人的外衣走了出去。

ENGLISH: The brook runs shallow and cold through the valley floor. David kneels and turns over stones until he finds five that sit perfectly in his palm.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 溪水又浅又凉，从谷底穿过。大卫跪下去，在石缝里翻找，直到摸到五块正好握在手心的石子。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: Five smooth stones. People love to guess what the five mean — the five books of the Law, five wounds, five something. The text simply says five smooth stones. Sometimes the honest reading is the better one.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 五块光滑的石子。有人爱猜「五」是什么意思——五卷律法、五处伤口。经文只说：五块光滑的石子。

SPEAKER: david
ENGLISH: He is a man, and I am a man. But he comes with a sword and a spear and a shield — and I come in the name of the LORD of hosts.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「他是人，我也是人；他靠的是刀、枪、盾牌，我靠的是万军之耶和华的名。」

ENGLISH: David looks at you. “Will you stand with me until the line?”
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 大卫回头看你：「你愿意陪我走到阵前吗？」

ENGLISH: Kneel and pray with him before he runs
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 跪下和他一起祷告

ENGLISH: The two of you bow beside the water. No thunder, no sign — just a quiet certainty that you are not the centre of this story.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你们一起在水边伏下身。没有雷声，也没有异象，你心里却安静地知道一件事：你不是这个故事的中心。

ENGLISH: Pick up a stone of your own and hold it tight
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 自己也捡一块石头，握紧

ENGLISH: The stone is ordinary. That is the strange part. God has always liked using ordinary things.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 那块石子普通得有点可笑。可妙就妙在这里——神一向喜欢用普通的东西。

ENGLISH: Step back and let him go alone
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 退一步，让他自己去

ENGLISH: You watch him walk down into the valley. Some roads can only be walked by one person at a time.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你看着他走下山谷。有些路，只能一个人走。

SPEAKER: goliath
ENGLISH: Am I a dog, that thou comest to me with staves? Come to me, and I will give thy flesh unto the fowls of the air and to the beasts of the field!
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「我岂是狗呢，你竟拿杖来攻击我？来吧，我要把你的肉给空中的飞鸟、田野的走兽吃！」

SPEAKER: david
ENGLISH: Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「你来攻击我，是靠刀枪和盾牌；我来攻击你，是靠万军之耶和华的名。」

ENGLISH: David runs toward the line. He reaches into his bag. The whole valley seems to hold its breath — and Corin grips your sleeve.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 大卫朝阵前跑去，手伸进袋子。整座山谷好像一下子屏住了呼吸——柯林抓紧你的袖子。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: Do not look away. Whatever you do, do not look away.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「别移开眼睛。不管发生什么，都别移开。」

ENGLISH: The stone sinks into the giant’s forehead. Goliath falls face down into the dust of the valley he had mocked for forty days.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 石子陷进巨人的额头。歌利亚脸朝下，扑倒在他骂了四十天的那片尘土里。

ENGLISH: The Philistine line breaks. The army of Israel finds its voice all at once.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 非利士人的阵线一下子散了，以色列全军在同一刻找回了声音。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: And there it is. Not a story about a boy beating a giant. A story about a God who keeps His promises — and a boy who knew Whose battle it was.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 这从来不是「小男孩打败大巨人」的故事，而是一位守约的神，和一个知道这场仗不属于自己的少年。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: Come. The road goes on, and the scroll is already turning.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 书卷自己翻过一页。前面的路还在。
